children: The Swiss market's defensive profile could appeal to investors after the U.S. midterm elections, though a stronger Swiss franc might temporarily limit the benefit, Vontobel's Jean-Philippe Bertschy says in a research note. "AI hubs, such as Texas, could see slower construction of new data centers," Bertschy says. This, in turn, could be a boon for sectors viewed as defensive by investors, as investment flows shift away from AI-related sectors due to uncertainty, he says. However, the prospect of a stronger Swiss franc relative to the dollar could temporarily weigh on earnings, according to Vontobel. Switzerland's SMI index closed at 14743 points on Tuesday, up 11% since the start of the year. (adria.calatayud@wsj.com)
